articles.title: How to send TradingView alerts to a webhook: JSON messages, placeholders and a Python receiver
articles.excerpt: A webhook turns a TradingView alert into an HTTP request to a server you choose: your own bot, a Telegram relay or a service that places orders with a broker. Setting it up takes five minutes. Getting…
articles.body: A webhook turns a TradingView alert into an HTTP request to a server you choose: your own bot, a Telegram relay or a service that places orders with a broker. Setting it up takes five minutes. Getting it to work reliably takes knowing a few rules that the alert dialog doesn't show: which placeholders need quotes, when TradingView sends JSON and when it sends plain text, which ports it accepts and how long it waits for an answer. This guide goes from the alert dialog to a receiver that runs. The TradingView facts come from its help pages, the Python receiver was run and tested, and the Pine Script passes Edgoro Pine Check. What you need A TradingView plan with webhooks (a paid plan) and two-factor authentication turned on: TradingView only allows webhook alerts on accounts with 2FA.
articles.author: Walid Koussa

articles.title: SoduWork Custom Model Setup: Connect an OpenAI-Compatible Gateway and Handle the 180-Second Stall
articles.excerpt: You install SoduWork, open the chat, and the model picker is empty. What is missing? A model service. SoduWork is an agent workbench that ships without a language model, so it only works after you con…
articles.body: You install SoduWork, open the chat, and the model picker is empty. What is missing? A model service. SoduWork is an agent workbench that ships without a language model, so it only works after you connect one. On November 16, 2026, I connected an OpenAI-compatible gateway to SoduWork v1.13.16 on Windows, and both gpt-6-sol and claude-haiku-5-5 appeared in the picker. The short version: add a service under My models , give it an API URL ending in /v1 , set the protocol to OpenAI compatible, paste a key, and register each Model ID by hand. This post is for developers who already have an API key and want to switch models inside SoduWork. If your team already provides a preconfigured gateway, skip to the last section on a 180-second stall I hit during a chat.

articles.title: Building an AI Agent Backend with FastAPI: From User Request to AI Response

articles.body: AI agents are becoming an interesting part of modern application development. A few years ago, most backend applications followed a straightforward approach. A user sent a request, the backend processed it using predefined logic, and the application returned a response. But things are changing. Today, applications can understand user instructions, decide what action to take, interact with external tools, retrieve information, and generate responses based on the results. This is where AI agents come into the picture. But have you ever wondered how a frontend application actually communicates with an AI agent? One practical way to build this connection is by using FastAPI .

articles.excerpt: "I'm not interested" is the most common reply on a cold call, and the way you handle it in the next five seconds decides whether the call ends or turns into a real conversation. These cold calling tip…
articles.body: "I'm not interested" is the most common reply on a cold call, and the way you handle it in the next five seconds decides whether the call ends or turns into a real conversation. These cold calling tips and sales scripts are for SDRs and BDRs on the phones every day, founders doing founder-led sales who hate cold outreach, and engineers or solutions engineers who just got handed a list and a dialer. This is objection handling for the moment before there's even a conversation to handle. The key thing to understand: "not interested" on a cold call is almost never a considered decision. The prospect doesn't know enough about you to be uninterested. It's a reflex, the same way "just looking" is a reflex in a shop. Your job isn't to argue with it.

articles.title: My Agent Picks a Free AI Model for You. How Do You Know It's Telling the Truth?
articles.excerpt: My Agent Picks a Free AI Model for You. How Do You Know It's Telling the Truth? By Rudi Tabuti (@bahjoe5) This article is my entry for the Creator Track of zkVerify Agent Games, Season 01. #AgentGames…
articles.body: My Agent Picks a Free AI Model for You. How Do You Know It's Telling the Truth? By Rudi Tabuti ( @bahjoe5 ) This article is my entry for the Creator Track of zkVerify Agent Games, Season 01. #AgentGames My agent routes your prompt to a free AI model and tells you which one answered. It picks the best-rated free model that can handle your request, and if that provider refuses, it fails over to the next one. It does this well: across three practice trials it scores 99 out of 100. Here is the problem I kept coming back to while building it: every one of those claims is self-reported. The agent says it routed you to the top-rated model. The agent says the first provider refused and it failed over. The agent says the answer came back verbatim. You have no way to check any of it.

articles.title: P vs NP for developers who never learned it, and what the AI 3-SAT news really means
articles.excerpt: Why I wrote this I watched a video about AI and "NP problems" and understood almost none of it. I've been a backend developer for years and had never heard of P vs NP. So I went back to zero and learn…
articles.body: Why I wrote this I watched a video about AI and "NP problems" and understood almost none of it. I've been a backend developer for years and had never heard of P vs NP. So I went back to zero and learned it one small step at a time. The deepest parts (how one problem is turned into another) still lost me, so this covers only what I actually understood. It's written for anyone starting where I started. Step 1: How fast is "fast"? Everything here depends on one idea: how the work grows when the input grows. Take n = 1,000 items: Growth Steps Feels like n 1,000 instant n² 1,000,000 instant n³ 1,000,000,000 about a second 2ⁿ a number with 302 digits never finishes The first three are polynomial : n multiplied by itself a fixed number of times.

articles.title: The part of the internet AI agents can't access
articles.excerpt: Over the last year agents got pretty good at the web. They can open a site, read it, click through a checkout, fill out a form. Tools like BrowserUse made that a lot more accessible, and honestly I th…
articles.body: Over the last year agents got pretty good at the web. They can open a site, read it, click through a checkout, fill out a form. Tools like BrowserUse made that a lot more accessible, and honestly I think that's great. For anything that lives in a browser, a browser agent is the right tool. The funny part is that when you look at your own day, a lot of it doesn't happen in a browser at all. You approve a bank transfer in the banking app. You reply to a supplier on WhatsApp. You check a delivery in some carrier app that has a website from 2012, if it has one. Plenty of services today are mobile first, and some are mobile only. There is no website you could point a browser agent at, and there is no public API either. So you end up with a strange situation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001.

articles.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
articles.excerpt: "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon. Everyone is very confident on this."
articles.body: For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold.

articles.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
articles.excerpt: This summer, comet 220P/McNaught burst into life out of nowhere to become one of the year’s highlights for amateur astronomers.
articles.body: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year.
